sentences: Matching asks for edges with disjoint endpoints, with perfect matching requiring every vertex to be covered.
Polynomial-time matching algorithms imply polynomial-size Boolean circuits for the decision problem.
The question asks whether general circuits can achieve logarithmic depth as well.
The cited source discusses a matching-size threshold and proves a strong depth lower bound when the circuit is required to be monotone.
The project is to understand whether allowing negation permits substantially shallower matching computations, beyond the restrictions captured by that monotone lower bound.
